tob-10785: Written by a colleague of Freud and Jung, this pioneering work argues that the strange symbols of alchemy — furnaces, kings, dragons — are really pictures of the human mind at work. Silberer reads alchemical texts as early attempts to describe psychological transformation. The book became a bridge between occult tradition and the new science of depth psychology.
tob-4085: Yeats’s 1903 book marks his turn from dreamy romance to a harder, plainer note. The title poem and its fellows draw on Ireland’s hero-age — Cuchulain and the old tales — while facing a present-day Ireland he found thin. The book stands at the hinge of his life’s work.
tob-0085: Fathered on the medieval schoolman Albertus Magnus, this spell-book of homely magic hoards charms, receipts, and privities for health, love, and warding. Handed down for centuries, it weds book-magic to peasant slyness. The book is a peephole on the people’s sorcery.
tob-4285: Budge’s Gods of the Egyptians — book one — is the great muster of Egyptian god-lore, naming the gods, their tales, and their worship. The British wonder-house’s Keeper of Egypt wrote with unmatched weight. The work opened old Egypt’s faith to common folk. A monument of young Egypt-lore.
tob-10485: Benedetto Croce’s Mystics of the Renaissance — in Frasci’s translation — studies the Italian mystics and what they mean for modern thought. The great thinker’s essays link Renaissance holy life with present-day ideas. The work is a fine piece of thought-history.
cia-0000105385: A September 1961 intelligence report on Aldo Moro's outlook for Italy's political future. Moro, a leading Christian Democrat who would later become prime minister, was navigating Cold War Italy's fragile coalition politics. The document captures American interest in a statesman whose life would end in the 1978 kidnapping and murder that shocked Italy — recorded here in his rising years.
cia-0000107285: Carrying an estimated publication date of November 1984, this report studies the changing role of Soviet-owned banks operating in the West. Moscow used these banks for trade finance — and, Western officials suspected, for moving money and gathering intelligence. The document shows Cold War competition extending into the quiet world of banking.
cia-0000107985: Estimated to date from March 1993, this is a supervisor's guide to the Employee Assistance Program — the CIA's internal counseling service for staff facing personal troubles. Even spies need help with stress, family problems, and substance abuse. The guide shows a rarely seen side of the agency: an employer looking after its people's welfare.
cia-0000118685: An estimated October 1965 document on Vietnam demonstrations — protests against the war, at home or abroad. As American troops poured into Vietnam, dissent was rising too. The entry shows the war's domestic front entering the intelligence picture.
cia-0000119585: An estimated November 1967 forecast of crisis in the Czechoslovak Communist Party. Analysts saw the storm gathering in Prague months before it broke. The document is prediction at its best — the Prague Spring, glimpsed on the horizon while it was still just weather.
cia-0000126885: A January 1968 warning, source deleted, of a possible second wave of Viet Cong attacks around February 18 — weeks after Tet began. The Tet Offensive's first shock was past; analysts feared the encore. The document is the war's intelligence pulse: expecting the next blow.
cia-0000126985: A June 1975 study of trends in communist media. What the bloc's press emphasized — and buried — revealed the party line's direction. The document is media criticism as intelligence: reading Pravda like a detective novel.
cia-0000127985: An April 1952 memorandum to the president transmitting Special Estimate 28 — the truncated title cuts off its subject. Hand-carrying an estimate to the White House marked it as urgent. The entry is the intelligence community's work at its most direct: analysts to president, no intermediaries.
cia-0000132185: Situation Report 502 on Soviet fears that the war would spread across the Persian Gulf — the truncated title suggests the rest. Moscow worried the conflict would ignite the whole region. The document shows the former superpower watching its old client burn, afraid of the fire spreading.
cia-0000132285: Situation Report 594: Saddam's one-two punch and worldwide reaction — the truncated title compresses the drama. The Iraqi leader's last gambits played to a global audience. The document is the finale's press coverage: the world, watching the end.
cia-0000132485: Item one in an April 1960 series: the Soviet bloc possibly preparing military aid to Cuba — the truncated title cuts off the details. Guns from the East would transform the Caribbean balance. The document is the first alarm: the island, about to be armed.
cia-0000132585: Item 3 in the September 1960 series: Latin American reactions to new American export restrictions on Cuba. The embargo was tightening, and the continent's capitals were choosing sides. The document tallies the responses: the neighbors, reacting.
cia-0000132685: A 1961 Latin America item: the situation in Cuba. The standing watch, continued. The document is the vigil: the island, monitored.
cia-0000135885: A 1952 file on Manuel G. — the middle name deleted. A person, partially named. The entry is the fragment: the man, half-identified.
cia-0000135985: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting information for SYNCARP on documents and materials — the truncated title cuts off which. The cryptonym guards the project. The entry is the request: the materials, itemized — the purpose, coded.
cia-0000136085: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the summit plan. The leadership meeting, arranged. The document is the plan: the summit, scheduled.
cia-0000138985: A 1946 military information report on Russian and Chinese communist activities in the Three Eastern Provinces — the archive's spelling says ThreeE, the truncated title cuts off the rest. Manchuria, covered. The document is the provinces: the activities, mapped.
un-ga-res-a-69-85: Resolution A/69/85, adopted in 2016 — the session's long tail. The designation and year are preserved; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1585: Security Council Resolution 1585, adopted in 2005 — aligned. The new year's Council deciding. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1785: Security Council Resolution 1785, cataloged with the year 2003 — the numbering suggests 2007, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-2085: Security Council Resolution 2085, adopted in December 2012 — the Mali resolution, authorizing an African-led force to help the government retake the north from militants. The Council backed Africa's answer to the jihadist advance. The resolution is the authorization: the force, African-led.
cia-0000132785: A 1960 CIA file on Cuban developments, numbered 0000132785. The revolution's paper trail, unbroken. The document is the trail: the year, covered.
cia-0000136685: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136685. The exiles' own words, archived. The document is the archive: the words, theirs.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d85: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 2, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 85. London wrote too. The message is the pair: two letters, one day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d185: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the President, November 2 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 185. Moscow's embassy reported. The cable is Moscow's: Harriman, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d285: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 22, 1943 — Document 285. Washington to Moscow. The message is the letter: the president, to the marshal.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d385: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the director of war mobilization — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 385. The insider wrote the mobilizer. The memo is the insider's: Hopkins, to Byrnes.
memoirs-of-sir-wemyss-reid-1842-1885: T. Wemyss Reid, the noted journalist, looks back on his busy life from 1842 to 1885 — newspapers, politics, and the literary world he knew. His memoirs are full of good stories and shrewd judgments. A lively Victorian self-portrait. Editors, statesmen, and men of letters pass through these lively, well-told recollections.
the-renascence-of-hebrew-literature-1743: Nahum Slouschz tells how Hebrew woke from sleep between 1743 and 1885 — poets and thinkers of the Haskalah giving new life to an old tongue. His book was the first to chart this rebirth for scholars. A landmark of Jewish literary history, still cited.
arxiv-2605-08785: Video playback and AI inference tolerate small arithmetic errors if the chip runs faster and cooler for it. Pragun Jaswal, L. Hemanth Krishna, and B. Srinivasu design a reconfigurable multiplier for the open RISC-V processor core that dials precision up or down depending on what the application can stomach. The 2026 paper is hardware research aimed at thriftier, cheaper silicon.
arxiv-2605-08885: Foundation models for chemistry must respect rotation — a molecule's energy does not change when you turn it — which is what SO(3) equivariance guarantees. Chen Wang, Siyu Hu, Guangming Tan, and Weile Jia make such atomistic models compact through structural pruning, cutting size while keeping the symmetry. The 2026 paper targets lean, physics-honoring models of matter.
arxiv-2605-08985: Multimodal models that see in ultra-high definition drown in pixels; encoding them efficiently is the bottleneck. Kechen Fang, Yihua Qin, Chongyi Wang, and colleagues ask what actually makes visual encoding efficient in the fourth version of LLaVA-UHD. The 2026 paper dissects efficient vision for multimodal LLMs.
arxiv-2605-09085: Estimating probability densities comes in two flavors — continuous and discrete — usually handled separately. Zhijun Zeng, Yixuan Jiang, Pipi Hu, and Zuoqiang Shi unify them with constant-target energy matching. The 2026 paper is a single unified framework for both worlds of density estimation.
arxiv-2605-09185: AI trading agents will face liars — fake news, planted rumors — and someone must test their gullibility first. Zhiwei Liu, Yangyang Yu, Yupeng Cao, and colleagues build AutoRedTrader, which red-teams trading agents by injecting synthetic misinformation. The 2026 paper is adversarial testing for financial AI.
arxiv-2605-09385: Tensor networks simulate quantum systems, but loops make truncation treacherous — naive cuts destroy the physics. Jacek Dziarmaga truncates loopy tensor networks by zero-mode gauge fixing, demonstrated on Z2 lattice gauge theory. The 2026 paper is computational quantum physics with a surgical truncation technique.
arxiv-2605-09885: The spin Seebeck effect converts heat into spin current; compensated ferrimagnets in magnetic junctions host it in intriguing ways. Xin Theng Lee, Takahiro Misawa, Mamoru Matsuo, and Takeo Kato investigate. The 2026 paper is spintronics on heat-driven spin currents in junctions.
arxiv-2605-09985: Humans compress abstractions prospectively — anticipating what will be needed before it arrives. Leonardo Hernandez Cano, Ivan Zareski, Luisa El Amouri, and colleagues study prospective compression in human abstraction learning. The 2026 paper is cognitive science on thinking ahead. It studies the mind's forward-looking compression.
arxiv-2605-10085: Accessible communication in a mixed-ability non-profit — designing for collective access, not individual accommodation. Xinru Tang and Anne Marie Piper search for solutions. The 2026 paper is accessibility design with a collective spirit. It designs for everyone together, collectively.
plos-pone-0003385: Not all body fat behaves alike, as this 2008 obesity study shows. Comparing gene activity in belly fat around the organs (visceral) versus fat under the skin (subcutaneous) in obese subjects, the researchers found different control programs for metabolism and the surrounding tissue matrix. The results help explain why deep belly fat carries greater health risks than fat under the skin.
plos-pone-0003485: Vaccine researchers found newborns vary in their shot response in this 2008 study. The BCG tuberculosis vaccine is given at birth, and the team measured natural differences in babies' immune responses to it. Understanding that variation matters for designing better TB vaccines, since BCG's patchy protection leaves adult lung disease as the big unsolved target.
plos-pone-0003585: Epidemiologists read a killer bug's last meals in this 2008 forensic study. Knowing which animals Chagas disease vectors bite is key to stopping the parasite's spread, and the team used DNA analysis of the insects' blood meals, demonstrated in Triatoma, to map feeding patterns. The method turns the bug's gut into an informant on transmission.
plos-pone-0003685: In 2008, Durand, Naidoo, and Coetzer used evolution to hunt malaria drug targets. Comparing Plasmodium proteins across species, their patterning approach flagged sites that evolution kept unchanged, the spots a drug could grip without quick resistance. The method turns the parasite's own history into a drug-hunting guide.
plos-pone-0003785: McGowan, Hogg, and Campbell brought librarians to the exam room in this 2008 trial. Their just-in-time information service fed rapid research answers to primary-care doctors during patient hours. The randomized test showed timely evidence sharpening everyday medical decisions.
plos-pone-0003885: Working in 2008, a team linked a virus to meningitis bacteria in young adults. A bacteriophage, a virus that infects bacteria, was found associated with meningococcal disease. The phage connection suggests the usually harmless throat germ turns nasty with viral help.
plos-pone-0003985: In 2008, Tokuda, Jimba, and Yanai linked trust to well-being in Japan. Their cross-sectional study tied interpersonal trust to quality-of-life scores. People who trusted others more reported clearly better subjective well-being overall. The finding treats social trust as a public-health asset worth building.
plos-pone-0004085: In 2008, Eldin, Ismail, and Mansour tracked acute hepatitis C in Egypt. They measured spontaneous viral clearance after symptomatic acute hepatitis infection. A delayed 12-week treatment course was also tested. The careful study guides when to treat and when to wait.
plos-pone-0004185: In 2009, Marshall and Hill caught a killer singing lies. An Australian predatory katydid mimicked cicada calls to lure prey. The aggressive mimic copied the victim's own signals. The deception shows ears can be weapons. The hunter's song turns the prey's ears against it.
plos-pone-0004285: In 2009, Cunningham, Fonager, and Jarra watched malaria genes switch coats. Transcription profiles of the yir multigene family shifted rapidly in cloned parasites. The variant antigens reshuffled fast. The speed explains immune evasion. The rodent malaria model mirrors human Plasmodium tricks.
plos-pone-0358885: Athletes stretch three ways — dynamic, static, and PNF — but which actually extends range of motion? This study compared all three on local and non-local flexibility and on when pain sets in during a stretch. The head-to-head results give trainers evidence-based rules for choosing a stretching method.
plos-pone-0357185: When teenagers in France develop mysterious fatigue and pain, Lyme disease often gets blamed — rightly or not. This multicenter study explored how adolescents and their parents perceive and experience suspected Lyme borreliosis. The social representations it maps reveal why the diagnosis divides families, doctors, and public health.
plos-pone-0357285: A child’s hearing loss caught late can cost them language itself. This study surveyed mothers of 1–5-year-olds on their knowledge and attitudes about childhood hearing loss. The gaps it found show where awareness campaigns must go to catch deafness early.
plos-pone-0358485: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors keep myeloproliferative neoplasms in check — but only if patients take them. This paper published a protocol for a mixed-methods systematic review of modifiable determinants of adherence. Mapping what can be changed sets up interventions that keep patients on their life-saving pills.
plos-pone-0353485: The Herculaneum scrolls — carbonized by Vesuvius — may hold lost classical texts. This paper showed a model carbonized papyrus scroll opens a novel path to identifying which scrolls of the Herculaneum Library are readable. The method could finally tell scholars which lumps of charcoal are worth unrolling virtually.
plos-pone-0357785: Spotting behavior disorders in preschoolers starts with asking parents the right questions. This paper gave a psychometric evaluation of a DSM-5-based semi-structured parent interview for externalizing disorders in young children. The validation tells clinicians whether the interview truly measures what it claims — and can be trusted in the clinic.
plos-pone-0357585: A high AUROC score can mask catastrophic decision failures in medical AI. This paper showed that in sepsis transcriptomic classifiers, preprocessing stability outweighs post hoc calibration across cohorts. The finding reframes how the field should evaluate clinical AI — robustness first, shiny metrics second.
plos-pone-0355285: Enzymes can be harnessed to destroy pharmaceutical pollutants in water. This paper built immobilized horseradish peroxidase hybrid biocatalysts for degrading pharmaceuticals and other emerging micropollutants. The reusable biocatalysts offer a green way to clean drug residues from wastewater.
plos-pone-0352885: Ancient metalwork along the Amber Road corridor traces the birth of elites. This paper followed socioeconomic change and emerging elites in the 4th–3rd century BCE through their metalwork. The artifacts map how power concentrated — written in bronze, gold, and iron.
plos-pone-0356285: High-fat diet mice develop the nerve damage of diabetes — a crucial model for testing treatments. This paper characterized diabetic peripheral neuropathy in that mouse model in detail. The thorough characterization gives drug developers a validated platform for screening new therapies.
plos-pone-0357385: Repeated exposure to the pesticide methyl bromide damages nerves and muscles. This paper studied the neuromuscular effects of that repeated exposure in detail. The findings quantify an occupational harm that regulators and farmworkers need to confront with hard numbers.
plos-pone-0356785: Thriving in the digital age demands soft skills, emotional intelligence, cognitive flexibility, and self-directed learning — but how do they connect? This cross-sectional study explored the structural relationships among all four. The resulting model maps the architecture of modern competence for educators and employers.
plos-pone-0356485: Germany’s approved digital health apps (DiGAs) are often evaluated with ultra-short questionnaires. This scoping review protocol will systematically map the use of single-item scales in DiGA evaluation. The planned review asks whether one question can really capture a health app’s worth.
plos-pone-0356885: Vascular dementia’s cognitive fog might lift with help from a traditional Chinese medicine compound. This rat study showed tanshinone IIA attenuates cognitive impairment in vascular dementia by modulating copper homeostasis via the SLC31A1/FDX1 axis. The copper-metabolism mechanism opens a novel therapeutic angle.
plos-pone-0354585: Spiramycin antibiotics polluting waterways need breaking down — and light plus catalysts can do it. This paper studied spiramycin degradation with a WO3 photocatalyst, using an XGBoost machine learning model to screen process parameters. The AI-optimized process points toward cleaner water.
plos-pone-0356685: Half-million-volt DC cables live or die by their electric field distribution. This paper examined how semiconductive shielding protrusions disturb the field in ±500 kV HVDC cables. The findings guide cable manufacturers toward designs that won’t fail catastrophically under load.
plos-pone-0355685: Antenatal care saves newborn lives — but which models work best in poor countries? This DHS-based propensity score matching analysis estimated the effect of antenatal care models on birthweight across low- and middle-income countries. The findings tell health ministries which prenatal care investments actually produce heavier, healthier babies.
plos-pone-0356385: Deep UV light can stiffen soft silicone — a useful trick for microdevices. This paper characterized the stiffening using nanoindentation. The precise mechanical measurements let engineers tune silicone stiffness with light — patterning hard and soft regions on a single chip.
plos-pone-0355385: Median U-turn intersections — replacing direct left turns — are spreading, but their performance across traffic levels needed testing. This scenario-based operational evaluation assessed them across demand levels. The findings tell traffic engineers when these unconventional intersections genuinely outperform traditional designs.
plos-pone-0353785: Everyone has frustration triggers — but they differ wildly between people. This paper profiled individual differences in frustration triggers and affective responses — the ‘boiling points’ study. The psychological profiles reveal why the same setback enrages one person and barely registers for another.
plos-pone-0355485: Diagnosing tuberculous pleurisy — TB fluid around the lung — is notoriously difficult. This paper published the protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of cell-free DNA’s diagnostic utility. The planned synthesis will determine whether a blood test can replace invasive pleural biopsy.
plos-pone-0354385: Geothermal fields of medium and low temperature — like Wenquan County’s — form through mechanisms worth understanding. This paper investigated their genesis mechanisms in Xinjiang. The geological findings guide the hunt for clean geothermal energy in similar terrains.
europmc-pmc2808385: Some people with HIV make antibodies that kill many strains, a gold clue for shots. This 2010 paper sifts memory B cells from HIV carriers and pulls out new antibodies with wide killing reach. The team maps each one's weak spot on the virus. Each find marks a bullseye for future jabs.
europmc-pmc2914085: Chiefs cannot wait years for proof roundups. This 2010 paper looks at fast-track reviews, how they are done, and what they risk. The authors weigh haste against care in method. Their take guides quick yet honest evidence for busy decision-makers.
europmc-pmc2919785: Dogs vary wildly in shape, yet the genetics are simple. This 2010 paper shows a simple genetic architecture underlies morphological variation in dogs. The authors find a few genes explain much of the difference. Their work made dogs a model for gene mapping.
europmc-pmc3004885: Bacterial genomes need crowd-scale study. This 2010 paper brings BIGSdb, a database for comparing germ genomes across whole populations. The authors' tool became a typing staple. It spread through labs worldwide. Outbreak hunters trace strains with it daily. Meningitis tracking leans on the database.
europmc-pmc3044685: Celiac and arthritis share gene spots. This 2011 gene trawl finds fourteen shared risk spots outside HLA in the two diseases. The authors reveal the overlap. Their work points to shared therapies. One pill might calm both conditions. The immune system misfires in similar ways.
europmc-pmc3045385: Stressed leukemia cells shed decoy bubbles. This 2011 paper shows heat and oxidant stress makes blood-cancer cells shed immune-dulling bubbles. The authors reveal the decoys. Their work points to immunotherapy. The bubbles blunt killer T cells. Blocking the shedding may unmask tumors.
europmc-pmc3074985: Sharp minds can harbor Alzheimer's plaques. This 2010 paper finds amyloid buildup in cognitively healthy elders. The authors reveal the paradox of reserve. Their work reframes Alzheimer's. Education seemed to buffer the damage. The finding reshaped prevention trials. Reserve is now a trial target.
europmc-pmc3079585: The genome got a user's guide. This 2011 ENCODE guide explains the encyclopedia of DNA elements. The consortium demystified the genome's dark matter. Their work trained biologists. Eighty percent of DNA showed activity. The guide remains the starting point. Critics debated the activity claims.
europmc-pmc6524685: Every branch of life - archaea, bacteria, and eukaryotes - sheds tiny membrane bubbles into its surroundings. This review tours extracellular vesicles across all three domains, plus the strange nanotubes some cells trail behind them. Though the bubbles' construction differs by domain, their roles in communication and cargo transport look universal, hinting at ancient origins.
europmc-pmc6645485: When researchers rate the same thing twice - or compare raters - the intraclass correlation (ICC) measures agreement. This paper revisits ICC theory with simulations, offering a simplified recipe for choosing and computing the right flavor. A clearer guide to a statistic everyone uses and few fully grasp.
europmc-pmc6653385: Some dying cancer cells do the immune system a favor - dying in a way that sounds the alarm. This review covers immunogenic cell death: the danger signals dying cells broadcast and the drugs that trigger this helpful demise. Turning tumor death into an immune rally could supercharge therapy.
europmc-pmc6658985: Depression and crushing fatigue often travel with chronic illness - and inflammation may be the thread. This review examines how immune-driven inflammation fuels low mood and exhaustion, especially in the already sick. Taming inflammation, the authors suggest, could lift two of medicine's most disabling symptoms.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-185: GAO, the watchdog that audits federal work, wrote this 2007 report on keep-the-lights-on plans for a national crisis. Auditors watched agencies test their backup plans during a 2006 drill that spanned the whole government. The report grades what worked, flags what flopped, and tells Congress which agencies still could not run if disaster struck.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1085: Big tanker spills were rare in 2007 — but GAO's report warns the cleanup fund was still exposed. One monster spill could swamp the federal oil-spill purse, the findings show. The report is a quiet alarm: good luck is not a funding strategy for the next Exxon Valdez.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-885: Airport building bills were piling up in 2007 — GAO's report eyes planned development costs, funding levels, and the administration's proposals. The findings give Congress the runway math. The report frames the airport question as a pay-for puzzle: grand plans, tight purses.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-585: Math could spot the killer trucks in 2007 — GAO's report says a statistical dragnet would finger the riskiest carriers better than gut feel. The findings pitch data over hunches. The report's promise: aim the inspectors where the numbers say the danger lives.
openalex-w7204971585: Toddlers and tablets are now inseparable, and this paper asks what heavy screen time does to very young children. The authors review evidence on how excessive exposure affects sleep, language development, and motor and cognitive milestones during the critical early years of brain maturation. The findings are cautionary without being alarmist. A research-backed resource for parents and pediatricians weighing how much screen is too much.
openalex-w7205013685: City budgets and school plans rarely speak the same language, but in Ilha Comprida, Sao Paulo, researchers checked whether they do. This article analyzes how the municipality's multi-year plans for 2022-2025 and 2026-2029 connect to the pedagogical projects of its schools. The authors trace the links between public planning and classroom reality. A rare, detailed look at whether government plans actually reach the school gate.
openalex-w7204563385: How children move says a lot about how they are developing. This study profiles the motor skills of elementary students at one institution, checking which children lag behind what is expected for their age. The authors link poor motor performance to gaps in surroundings and support. A developmental study that treats playground skills as a health signal.
openalex-w7163537885: Some metals act as if their electrons weighed hundreds of times too much. This lab paper hunts that odd heavy behavior in manganese crystals with magnetic scans. The team mapped the tiny electron states inside. A study of quantum oddity hiding in real metal.
openalex-w7213257185: Japan's deadliest downpours come from rain bands that stall in place. This paper studies the storm environments behind quasi-stationary linear rain systems tied to Baiu front lows. The authors dug into what sets the stage for these deluges. An atmospheric-science study of the recipe for Japan's worst floods.
pmc-13469185: In this 2026 microbiology methods paper, scientists built Universal-Bac3Gel, a 3D lab-grown matrix that lets dangerous ESKAPE bacteria form biofilms as they would in a real infection. Biofilms make germs far harder to kill, and having a realistic testbed accelerates the hunt for drugs that break them. The paper reports how the matrix was made and validated.
pmc-13458285: This 2026 neuroscience paper finds that sevoflurane, a common anesthetic gas, causes cognitive problems in aged rats through the PRKCD protein acting on the PINK1/Parkin mitophagy pathway — the cell's system for recycling worn-out mitochondria. The result helps explain post-surgery confusion in elderly patients and points to protective targets.
pmc-13453285: A 2026 qualitative study using focus groups to understand why people in rural communities do or don't join cancer clinical trials. Distance, trust, and logistics emerged as the real barriers. Hearing rural voices directly gives trial designers concrete ways to make research participation possible outside cities.
pmc-13549385: In this 2026 oncology study, researchers examined whether SGLT2 inhibitors — diabetes drugs that flush glucose through urine — are linked to better or worse outcomes in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Drug interactions in complex patients matter, and the association analysis gives oncologists one more factor to weigh.
pmc-13481985: In this 2026 drug development paper, scientists built and characterized a long-acting allosteric growth hormone receptor blocker for acromegaly, a disorder of excess growth hormone. Allosteric drugs bind away from the main site, and a long-acting version means fewer injections. The paper reports the molecule's design and testing.
pmc-13443285: A 2026 surgical outcomes paper comparing patients who did and didn't get a pouch after total proctocolectomy — removal of colon and rectum. The authors ask who skips the restorative pouch and how they fare. For patients facing this life-changing surgery, real data on both paths supports better decisions.
pmc-13442985: This 2026 endocrinology piece asks a direct question: can acromegaly — excess growth hormone, usually from a pituitary tumor — be controlled in every case? The authors review why some patients resist standard treatment and what options remain. It is an honest accounting of the limits of current therapy.
pmc-13440985: A 2026 paper describing the development and mixed-methods evaluation of "DiscoverU," an afterschool mentoring program for adolescent health and well-being. The formative study refined the program with input from teens themselves. It is a practical blueprint for building youth programs that actually engage.
pmc-13499685: A 2026 trial protocol for a technology-blended exercise intervention aimed at reducing cognitive risk and supporting brain health in middle-aged and older Singaporeans with type 2 diabetes. Diabetes raises dementia risk, and the study blends digital tools with physical activity. The paper lays out the intervention design.
pmc-13643785: A 2026 genetics paper identifying a "new" crystal/Su(Ste) locus on the fruit fly Y chromosome that resembles a piRNA cluster regulating Stellate repeats. The Y chromosome is gene-poor but full of surprises. The discovery adds a piece to the puzzle of how flies silence selfish genetic elements.
pmc-13382385: A 2026 medical physics paper on probabilistic quality assurance of biopsy DVH thresholds in high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy under localization uncertainty. When the target's exact position is uncertain, dose planning must account for it. The probabilistic approach makes the QA honest.
pmc-13487485: In this 2026 hematology paper, Stag2-dependent chromatin remodeling was shown to enforce the erythroid-specific Gata1 cistrome — the full set of DNA sites the Gata1 factor binds in red blood cell precursors. Chromatin structure dictates which genes the master regulator can reach. The mechanism clarifies red cell development.
pmc-13481685: A 2026 implementation study tailoring strategies for an acute coronary syndrome quality improvement program at the primary care level across eastern, western, and central China. One size doesn't fit all regions. The tailored strategies address local realities.
pmc-13454685: This 2026 (listed 2025) biogeography paper compared two South American sedge lineages across the Southern Cone — "a tale of two lineages." The comparative approach reveals shared and distinct histories. The Carex groups tell a continental story.
pmc-13631485: A 2026 Korean-language history paper on the formation of Korea's pre-medical school system and the instability of pre-medical education from 1945 to 1979. The institutional history is written for Korean readers. The paper traces how medical training took shape.
pmc-13448385: A 2026 conference abstract (TLSB-13) systematically reviewing and meta-analyzing the prognostic value of cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor DNA in NSCLC patients with CNS metastases. The liquid biopsy of the brain's fluid was evaluated. The meta-analysis is the evidence.
pmc-13404385: A 2026 call for papers on preparing an emergency-ready health workforce. The journal solicited the research. The entry preserves the call.
pmc-13463285: This 2026 review examined the mechanobiology of adipocyte hypertrophy — cytoskeletal remodeling as a driver of insulin resistance in obesity. The fat cell's mechanics caused metabolic harm. The driver is the mechanism.
pmc-13434185: A 2026 paleoanthropology paper on dietary adaptation in Paranthropus robustus postcanine teeth. The extinct hominin's diet was read from its teeth. The adaptation is the evolutionary story.
pmc-13430085: A 2026 motor control paper with eye tracking insights into movement preparation and execution under nonstandard visual movement feedback. The gaze revealed the motor planning. The insights are the finding.
pmc-13411285: In this 2026 review, microRNAs in spinal cord injury were examined — molecular and translational insights. The small RNAs' injury role was synthesized. The review is the roadmap.
pmc-13500785: A 2026 paper translating biosynthetic gene cluster architecture into biosensor design for microbial natural product discovery. The gene clusters became sensors. The translating is the synthetic biology.
pmc-13437085: A 2026 methods paper proposing a framework for two-way fixed effects models in air pollution epidemiology — model specifications and recommendations for future studies. The framework standardizes the field. The recommendations are the contribution.
